cards.name: Premiere audio scripting surface
cards.summary: What audio work in Premiere 26 can be automated from scripts, and what is UI-only. Scriptable: clip Volume Level (gain, fades, ducking keyframes), adding clip audio effects by name and setting their params, track mute, clip audio channel mapping (Modify > Audio Channels) on project items, export with a loudness-normalizing .epr. UI-only: everything in the Essential Sound panel (tagging, presets, Auto-Match, Auto Ducking, Enhance Speech, Repair/Clarity sliders, Remix), Audio Gain/Normalize dialog, Audio Track Mixer track effects, Loudness Meter readings, Separate Crosstalk, bleep/mute.
use_for: deciding which audio steps an automated edit can do
planning a VO + music mix without UI clicks
cards.how: ExtendScript DOM: app.project.sequences[i].audioTracks[t].clips[k].components -> 'Volume' (Level), 'Channel Volume', 'Panner'; ComponentParam.setValue/addKey/setValueAtKey/setTimeVarying. QE DOM adds effects to clips. UXP (Premiere 25.6+) has AudioFilterFactory, AudioComponentChain, AudioClipTrackItem, AudioTrack.setMute, ComponentParam actions, EncoderManager. AdobeBridge today exposes only audio[] gain_db / fade_in / fade_out (pr_build.jsx writes Volume Level keyframes); PVE check_spec validates clip effects against the VIDEO harvest, so audio effect names in a spec would be reported as unknown until audio support is wired.
cards.script_api: ExtendScript: TrackItem.components, ComponentParam.setValue(v, true)/addKey(t)/setValueAtKey(t, v, true)/setTimeVarying(true), Track.setMute(1)/isMuted(), ProjectItem.getAudioChannelMapping (attribute) + AudioChannelMapping.setMappingForChannel(ch, src) + ProjectItem.setAudioChannelMapping(mapping) (Adobe PProPanel sample; setter not in the community guide), Sequence.exportAsMediaDirect(out, epr, workArea); QE: qe.project.getAudioEffectList(), qe.project.getAudioEffectByName(name), QETrackItem.addAudioEffect(fx), qe.project.getAudioTransitionList() (all four used successfully by pve/harvest_pr.jsx on 26.x); UXP: AudioFilterFactory.getDisplayNames()/createComponentByDisplayName(name, item), AudioComponentChain.createAppendComponentAction/createInsertComponentAction/createRemoveComponentAction, AudioTrack.setMute(bool), ComponentParam.createKeyframe/createAddKeyframeAction/createSetValueAction, EncoderManager.exportSequence(seq, exportType, out, epr, exportFull) (all UXP calls listed are 'since 25.6', so they exist in the installed Premiere 26.0.2; 26.3+ additions such as AudioTrack.createSetNameAction do not)
cards.limits: QE is undocumented and unsupported. Stereo-only effects fail SILENTLY on mono clips: in the 2026-10-03 harvest (mono 32 kHz WAV) Channel Mixer, Balance, Swap Channels, Fill Left with Right, Fill Right with Left, Channel Volume and Stereo Expander were not added (the last component stayed 'Volume'); always re-read components[last].displayName after adding. Live wave 3 (2026-10-14) added all 53 audio effects to a stereo clip and dumped their real rows (pve/harvest/pr_audio_params_w3.json) and measured their 0..1 values in dB / Hz / s / LUFS (the pr_audio cards' params[].measured). getVideoEffectByName returns an object even for unknown names (README); assume the same for audio and check getAudioEffectList() first. Clip component keyframe times are in source-media seconds: add trackItem.inPoint.seconds (pr_build.jsx does). No Essential Sound API in ExtendScript or in the UXP reference as of 26.5 (absence = not found, not confirmed by Adobe). The Premiere Scripting Guide says ExtendScript is supported 'through September 2026' while Adobe's Sept 2026 UXP blog says ExtendScripts are not affected by the CEP retirement; it still runs in the installed Premiere 26.0.2 on 2026-10-03, but plan UXP ports.

cards.name: Premiere audio effect parameter scale (scripts)
cards.summary: Through ExtendScript/QE every Premiere audio-effect parameter reads and writes as a normalized 0..1 number, not the dB/ms/% the UI shows. Linear params map as (ui - min) / (max - min). The intrinsic clip Volume 'Level' is the exception: linear amplitude where 0 dB = 10^(-15/20).
use_for: converting a dB/ms target into a pr_props value
cards.how: Verified against Adobe's documented defaults vs harvested defaults: Automatic Click Remover Threshold 30 (1..100) -> 0.2929, Complexity 16 -> 0.1515; Single-band/Multiband Compressor Threshold 0 dB (-60..0) -> 1.0, Attack 10 ms (0..500) -> 0.02, Release 100 ms (0..5000) -> 0.02, Single-band 'Gain' 0 dB (-30..+30) -> 0.5; Tube-modeled 'Gain' 0 dB (-18..+18) -> 0.5; Pitch Shifter 'Transpose Ratio' 1.0 (0.5..2.0) -> 0.3333; Graphic EQ bands 0.5 = 0 dB. Volume 'Level' = 10^((dB - 15) / 20): 0.1778 = 0 dB, 1.0 = +15 dB (Essential Sound clip volume range -60..+15 dB). Worked examples: compressor threshold -20 dB -> 0.6667; ratio 3:1 -> (3-1)/29 = 0.069; makeup +4 dB on Single-band 'Gain' -> 0.5667. In a PVE spec: {"name": "Single-band Compressor", "pr_props": {"Threshold": 0.6667, "Ratio": 0.069, "Attack": 0.02, "Release": 0.02, "Gain": 0.5667}}.
cards.script_api: trackItem.components[n].properties[i].getValue() / setValue(normalized, true); for Volume: comp('Volume').properties 'Level' setValue(Math.pow(10, (dB - 15) / 20), true) (pr_build.jsx)
cards.limits: Frequency and some time params are NOT linear (Parametric EQ band centres 0.0019..0.80, DeHummer base 0.002, Highpass Cutoff 0.25): their mapping is unverified, so do not compute them; read a value set in the UI with getValue() first, or leave defaults. Popup params (Mode, Type) are stored as fractions whose index mapping is unverified. Ratio mapping (r-1)/29 is inferred from the documented 1..30 range. Values outside 0..1 are clamped.

cards.name: Essential Sound panel
cards.summary: Task-based audio panel: tag each clip Dialogue, Music, SFX or Ambience and get type-specific one-slider tools. Sections per type (from the installed PremiereAdjustmentsModes.json): Dialogue = Enhance Speech, Loudness, Repair, Clarity, Creative (Reverb), Clip Volume; Music = Loudness, Duration (Remix), Ducking, Clip Volume; SFX = Loudness, Creative, Pan, Clip Volume; Ambience = Loudness, Creative, Stereo Width, Ducking, Clip Volume.
use_for: music bed ducking and length fitting
cards.how: Window > Essential Sound (Audio workspace). Select clip(s) in the Timeline, choose the type (or Auto Tag), then use a Preset or the section sliders (0-10). Settings are stored as regular audio effects in the clip's stack (documented for Ducking -> Amplify; inferred for the rest from preset data, see the Repair/Clarity/Creative cards). Save the state as a preset with the icon next to the Preset menu.
cards.script_api: none (no ExtendScript or UXP API found for audio type, presets or ES sliders; replicate with the standalone effects listed on the Repair, Clarity and Reverb cards)
cards.limits: UI-only; per clip, not per track; one type per clip. Changing ES volume while previewing with Timeline Sync changed sequence levels: fixed in 26.2, so the installed Premiere 26.0.2 still has it (avoid ES volume edits during Timeline Sync preview).

cards.name: Auto Tag (audio category tagging)
cards.summary: AI classifier that labels selected clips as Dialogue, Music, SFX or Ambience and adds clickable Essential Sound badges to the clips.
use_for: tagging a whole rough cut before Auto-Match or Ducking
letting ducking know which clips are dialogue
cards.how: Select clips in the Timeline > Essential Sound > Auto Tag. Badges appear on clips; click a badge to open its section. The classifier models ship in Settings/EssentialSound (SoundClassifier.json, Classifier_Speech_Music_Other.json).
cards.script_api: none
cards.limits: UI-only; check results: news clips with music under speech may be mis-tagged. Ducking needs the driving clips tagged.

cards.name: Essential Sound presets
cards.summary: Factory one-click presets per audio type. Installed list (2026-10-03): Dialogue - Background Walla Walla, Balanced High Tone Voice, Balanced Low Tone Voice, Clean Up Noisy Dialogue, From Outside a Building, From the Radio, From the Telephone, From the Television, In a Large Room, In a Small Room, Make Close Up, Make Distant, Make Medium Shot, Over the Intercom, Podcast Voice. Music - Balanced Background Music, Duck against everything, Hard Vocal Ducking, Smooth Vocal Ducking, Remix to 30/60/90 Seconds. SFX - Explosion, From Outside, From the Left, From the Right, In a Large Room, Make Close Up, Make Distant, Make Medium Shot. Ambience - Focused, From Outside, Room Tone, Wide and Deep.
use_for: 'Podcast Voice' or 'Clean Up Noisy Dialogue' as a VO starting point
'From the Telephone'/'From the Radio' for phone-call or archive-radio recreations
cards.how: Essential Sound > choose type > Preset menu. Presets are JSON files (.essentialsound) in %APPDATA%\Adobe\Premiere Pro\26.0\EssentialSound\Default\<dialog|music|sfx|ambience|generic>\; '(Config)' holds the defaults/ranges, '(Default)' the reset state. User presets are saved from the panel.
cards.script_api: none (files can be read for reference values; applying a preset needs the panel)
cards.limits: Preset file format is undocumented; editing/adding files is unsupported. Applying a preset overwrites the clip's ES settings.

cards.name: Loudness Auto-Match
cards.summary: Essential Sound > Loudness > Auto-Match sets each clip to a per-type integrated loudness so cuts do not jump in level. Installed default targets (from (Config).essentialsound): Dialogue -23 LUFS, Music -25 LUFS, SFX -21 LUFS, Ambience -30 LUFS, untagged -24 LUFS (allowed range -42..-12 LUFS). The measured clip LUFS is shown under the button.
use_for: evening out interview/VO clips recorded at different levels
cards.how: Tag clips, select them, Essential Sound > Loudness > Auto-Match. Then mix relative levels with Clip Volume. Scripted equivalent (0 credits): measure each source's integrated LUFS (ffmpeg -af ebur128 or loudnorm print_format=json), gain_db = target - measured, write Volume Level = 10^((gain_db - 15)/20) (AdobeBridge audio[].gain_db does exactly this conversion).
cards.script_api: none; equivalent = ComponentParam 'Level' of the 'Volume' component via setValue (yes)
cards.limits: Clip-level normalization, not a mix master: the sum of VO + music will be louder than each target. -23 LUFS dialogue is a broadcast-style level, about 9 LU below web delivery (-14); push the final mix at export. Which internal property Auto-Match writes is unverified. Targets are not editable in Premiere's UI (Adobe PM note, 2017).

cards.name: Auto Ducking
cards.summary: Essential Sound > Ducking on a Music or Ambience clip computes volume dips wherever the chosen 'Duck Against' types (Dialogue, Music, SFX, Ambience, untagged) play. Premiere adds an Amplify effect and writes the keyframes to its Gain param.
use_for: reels where music must drop for each line
cards.how: Tag VO as Dialogue and music as Music. Select the music clip > Ducking > pick Duck Against icons > set Sensitivity, Duck Amount, Fade Duration, Fade Position (outside / inside / middle of dialogue) > Generate Keyframes. Factory preset values (music preset files, slot meaning inferred): default and 'Balanced Background Music' = sensitivity 6, fade 800 ms, duck -18 dB; 'Smooth Vocal Ducking' = 4, 1200 ms, -24 dB; 'Hard Vocal Ducking' = 7, 250 ms, -36 dB. Scripted equivalent: from the VO clip timings (or a VAD pass on the VO file) keyframe the music clip's Volume Level down 12-18 dB with 250-800 ms ramps, ramping back up after gaps longer than about 1 s (pr_build.jsx already writes Volume keyframes for fades).
cards.script_api: none for Generate Keyframes; equivalent = Volume 'Level' addKey/setValueAtKey (yes). Reading generated keyframes: Amplify 'Gain' via getKeys()/getValueAtKey() returns normalized values (0.6667 = 0 dB).
cards.limits: Pressing Generate Keyframes again overwrites manual keyframe edits. Only Music/Ambience clips can be ducked; the driving clips must be tagged. Bugs fixed after the installed 26.0.2, so still present there: crash ducking Music against many Dialogue clips (fixed 26.3), Save As Copy breaking ducking (fixed 26.3), deleted ducking keyframes still audible (fixed 26.5): to undo ducking, disable or delete the Amplify effect rather than deleting keyframes. See also: 'Scripted ducking from VO ranges'; 'Music ducks under VO (scripted, from VO ranges)'.

cards.name: Enhance Speech (Essential Sound)
cards.summary: On-device AI that rebuilds a dialogue recording to sound like a close studio mic (removes noise, room and muddiness). Runs in the background with a progress bar; a Mix Amount slider blends enhanced and original.
use_for: phone/lav interviews with room echo or traffic
AI-education VO recorded in an untreated room
cards.how: Select a Dialogue clip > Essential Sound > Enhance Speech > Enhance. Wait for processing (keeps editing). Back the Mix Amount off (partial blend sounds less synthetic). Add EQ/compression after it like any clip.
cards.script_api: none (no ExtendScript/UXP call found). Scriptable stand-ins: DeNoise + DeReverb via QE/UXP (yes); external batch tools outside Premiere if a clean file is needed (not part of PVE).
cards.limits: Mono and stereo only; no multichannel, no nested sequences; a stereo clip is returned as a MONO downmix. Slow on older hardware (Adobe example: 25 s to process a 5 s clip); recommended Apple M1+/macOS 13+ or a recommended GPU on Windows. Can sound processed or invent consonants on very bad sources: check by ear. Not a cloud feature (Adobe lists Separate Crosstalk as the only cloud AI voice feature).

cards.name: Essential Sound Repair (Reduce Noise, Rumble, DeHum, DeEss, Reduce Reverb)
cards.summary: Dialogue > Repair: five checkbox+slider (0-10) fixes. The installed (Config) file shows what each slider drives, which gives scriptable equivalents: Reduce Noise -> DeNoise 'Amount' 0..1; Reduce Reverb -> DeReverb 'Amount' 0..1 with 'Auto Gain' on; Reduce Rumble -> an FFT Filter high-pass curve (266 values); DeEss -> DeEsser params interpolated from 'Threshold' 0.875, 'Center Frequency' 0.191, 'Bandwidth' 0.257 (slider 0) to 0.5 / 0.261 / 0.527 (slider 10).
use_for: low rumble from traffic or handling (<80 Hz)
cards.how: Essential Sound > Dialogue > Repair > tick the fix > slider 0-10 (start 3-5, listen). Script stand-in: add the named effect with QE/UXP and set the mapped param, e.g. {"name": "DeNoise", "pr_props": {"Amount": 0.3}}.
cards.script_api: none for the panel; stand-ins DeNoise / DeReverb / DeEsser / FFT Filter / DeHummer are scriptable (see their cards)
cards.limits: Mapping read from preset data; that Repair adds exactly these effects is inferred (medium). DeHum's effect and its 50/60 Hz switch were not found in the config: use DeHummer or Notch Filter at 50 Hz for India.

cards.name: Essential Sound Clarity (Dynamics, EQ presets, Vocal Enhancer)
cards.summary: Dialogue > Clarity: Dynamics (Natural -> Focused compression/leveling), an EQ preset + Amount, and Vocal Enhancer (High Tone / Low Tone). The EQ presets are stored as 15-value arrays that match Graphic Equalizer (10 Bands) params exactly (Accuracy, Gain, Range, Reset, EQ Band 1-10, Is Processing), so they can be reproduced by script. Installed EQ presets: Background Voice, Intercom, Locked in the Trunk, Old Radio, On the Telephone, Outside of the Room, Podcast Voice, Subtle Boost (High Tone), Subtle Boost (Low Tone), That Public Radio Sound, Vocal Presence.
cards.how: UI: Essential Sound > Clarity > tick Dynamics / EQ / Vocal Enhancer. Script stand-in = 'Graphic Equalizer (10 Bands)' with values (EQ Band 1..10): Podcast Voice Range 0.3924, bands 0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5179, 0.5077, 0.5, 0.5179, 0.5281, 0.5103, 0.5; Vocal Presence Accuracy 0.0966, Range 0.3249, bands 0.3572, 0.3572, 0.4643, 0.4786, 0.4764, 0.4957, 0.5592, 0.5652, 0.5086, 0.4699; On the Telephone Range 0.3924, bands 0.3286 x4, 0.4857, 0.5307, 0.5307, 0.4836, 0.3286, 0.3286; Old Radio Range 0.7975, bands 0.1572 x3, 0.2844, 0.4832, 0.365, 0.5285, 0.4351, 0.2715, 0.1572. Other presets: read the array from dialog/(Config).essentialsound.
cards.script_api: none for the panel; stand-in = QE addAudioEffect('Graphic Equalizer (10 Bands)') + setValue per band (yes)
cards.limits: Clarity 'Amount' scaling between flat and the preset curve is not in the file (unverified, likely a blend). Vocal Enhancer here maps to the 'Vocal Enhancer' effect whose 'Mode' index mapping is unverified.

cards.name: Essential Sound Creative Reverb
cards.summary: Creative > Reverb adds a preset room with Amount and Clip Volume sliders. Presets are 13-value arrays that match Studio Reverb params in order (Low Frequency Cut, High Frequency Cut, Room Size, Width, Diffusion, Damping, Decay, Early Reflections, Early Reflections Delay, Dry Output Level, Wet Output Level, Is Processing, Number of Channels). Dialogue presets: Auditorium, Church, Large Reflective Room, Outside the Club, Small Dry Room, Thicken Voice, Warm Room, Warm Voice. SFX: Heavy Reverb, Light Reverb, Outside Reverb, Room Reverb. Ambience: Large Room Ambience, Outside Ambience, Room Ambience, Wind Effect.
use_for: matching dry VO to on-location sync sound
space on SFX hits in trailers
cards.how: UI: Essential Sound > Creative > Reverb > Preset + Amount. Script stand-in: 'Studio Reverb' with the preset array, e.g. Warm Voice = {"Low Frequency Cut": 0.196, "High Frequency Cut": 0.8999, "Room Size": 0, "Width": 0.4, "Diffusion": 0.2, "Damping": 0.4, "Decay": 0.102, "Early Reflections": 0.09, "Early Reflections Delay": 0.5, "Dry Output Level": 1, "Wet Output Level": 0.3}.
cards.script_api: none for the panel; stand-in = Studio Reverb via QE/UXP (yes)
cards.limits: Reverb on documentary VO is usually wrong: use it only to match a location or for a stylised effect. How 'Amount' scales Wet Output Level is unverified.

cards.name: Remix tool and Essential Sound Duration
cards.summary: AI retimes a music clip to a target duration by cutting and crossfading the middle at beat-compatible points, keeping the intro and ending. Usually within 1 s of the target (always within 5 s).
use_for: fitting a stock track to a 30/60/90 s reel
music ending exactly on the last frame of a trailer
re-fitting music after the cut changes length
cards.how: Toolbar: hold the Ripple Edit tool group > Remix Tool, drag the music clip's end to the new length; or Essential Sound > Music > Duration: Target Duration, Segments (fewer/more cuts), Variations (melodic vs harmonic). Zigzag marks show the edits. For a hit point mid-song, split there and remix both halves. Presets 'Remix to 30/60/90 Seconds' exist.
cards.script_api: none (no API found); fallback = cut and crossfade manually in the spec
cards.limits: Ignores lyrics: vocal tracks can splice lines from different verses. Remixing an Adobe Stock preview then licensing it can shift timing: re-apply on the licensed file. Not on read-only projects.

cards.name: Separate Crosstalk
cards.summary: Cloud AI that splits overlapping speakers in one clip into one track per speaker plus a background track; the original is disabled.
use_for: panel debates and TV-studio arguments where guests talk over each other
cards.how: Cut the clip down to the overlap (1 s to 10 min), then right-click > Separate Crosstalk (or Clip menu / Properties panel) > Separate. One clip at a time.
cards.script_api: none
cards.limits: Premium: 1 Generative Credit per second processed, plus an automatic 2 s handle each side. Requires sign-in and internet; uploads audio and voice embeddings to Adobe; consent needed; unavailable for files from Illinois or Texas. No default shortcut. Not in the installed Premiere 26.0.2 (no 'Crosstalk' UI string) and not named in the release notes or What's New through 26.5.2 (Adobe's help page dated 2026-07-28 documents it without a beta label): confirm it exists in the Clip menu after updating before planning on it.

cards.name: Bulk mute or bleep (censored word list)
cards.summary: Transcript-driven censoring: add words to a Censored word list, filter them in the Text panel and apply a bleep tone or mute to one or all hits.
use_for: bleeping abuse in political street interviews
cards.how: Transcribe the sequence > Text panel > More options > Censored word list (import/export lists supported) > Filter: Censored words > Apply dropdown: choose tone, apply to one or all instances.
cards.script_api: none for applying; UXP Transcript.transcribeClipProjectItem (since 25.6) can create transcripts; Transcript has no censor/bleep/mute call
cards.limits: Only as good as the transcript (check Hindi/Hinglish recognition). Shipped with the media-intelligence features (release notes 25.6; What's New lists it under 26.0); present in the installed 26.0.2 (Censored word list strings found).

cards.name: Generative Extend (audio)
cards.summary: Firefly-powered extension of a clip's head or tail; for audio it can add up to 10 s of continuing ambience or room tone (video up to 2 s).
use_for: room tone to cover a cut in an interview
letting ambience ring out under an end card
cards.how: Generative Extend tool, drag the clip edge. Original media is unchanged.
cards.script_api: none
cards.limits: Never extends spoken dialogue (dialogue is muted in the extension); music clips are not eligible; mono/stereo only (no 5.1); cloud model, needs sign-in/internet; uses generative credits. Bugs present in the installed 26.0.2: gain doubled on clips with audio gain (fixed 26.3), waveform offset when extending a clip head (fixed 26.5).

cards.name: Generative Media Tool (sound effects)
cards.summary: Generate sound effects (and video) from a text prompt inside the timeline, optionally guiding timing and intensity with your voice; results are added as editable clips.
cards.how: Generative Media Tool in the timeline: prompt, check the credit cost shown, generate, place the result.
cards.script_api: none
cards.limits: Uses generative credits (cost shown before generating); cloud, needs sign-in/internet. Added in 26.5 (September 2026): NOT in the installed Premiere 26.0.2 (no UI strings for it), so unavailable until Premiere is updated.

cards.name: Generate Music (beta)
cards.summary: Firefly Music model generates instrumental background music for a selected timeline range from a prompt and tempo, with variations and optional looping; 48 kHz clips, no vocals.
use_for: temp or final background beds when stock music does not fit
beds that match a cut's exact length
cards.how: Premiere (beta) only: select a range, describe the music, set tempo, generate, compare the four variations; results are kept in Generation history.
cards.script_api: none
cards.limits: Premiere (beta) app only, not the release 26.x; uses generative credits; instrumental only; Adobe states commercially safe, royalty-free use.

cards.name: Clip volume (Volume effect 'Level')
cards.summary: Every audio clip's intrinsic 'Volume' component ('Bypass', 'Level') sets clip level and carries fades and ducking keyframes. The main scriptable mixing control.
cards.how: UI: Effect Controls > Volume > Level, rubber band in the Timeline (Ctrl+click adds keyframes), Essential Sound Clip Volume. Script: Level = 10^((dB - 15)/20) (0.1778 = 0 dB, max 1.0 = +15 dB); keyframe times are source seconds: t_key = trackItem.inPoint.seconds + offset. AdobeBridge spec: audio[] {"src", "gain_db", "fade_in", "fade_out"}.
cards.script_api: prop = components['Volume'].properties['Level']; prop.setValue(lv, true); prop.setTimeVarying(true); prop.addKey(t); prop.setValueAtKey(t, lv, true) (verified in AdobeBridge pr_build.jsx); UXP (25.6+): ComponentParam.createSetTimeVaryingAction(true), createKeyframe(v) (set its position to a TickTime) + createAddKeyframeAction(kf), run inside project.executeTransaction
cards.limits: Mono clips get a further -3 dB pan law (AdobeBridge README). Fades written by pr_build are linear in the Level value. Track-level volume (mixer fader) is separate and not scriptable.

cards.name: Audio Gain dialog (Set / Adjust / Normalize peaks)
cards.summary: Clip gain applied before the Volume effect: Set Gain to, Adjust Gain by, Normalize Max Peak to, Normalize All Peaks to (dB), with the measured Peak Amplitude shown.
use_for: matching many clips' peaks at once (keyboard G)
cards.how: Select clips > right-click > Audio Gain (G). Normalize Max Peak to -1 dB for a peak ceiling; use Loudness Auto-Match or LUFS math for perceived loudness instead.
cards.script_api: none found in ExtendScript/UXP (unverified absence); use Volume 'Level' gain instead
cards.limits: Peak normalization is not loudness normalization.

cards.name: Audio Track Mixer (track effects, automation, submixes)
cards.summary: Per-track faders, pan, mute/solo, insert effects and sends, automation modes (Off, Read, Write, Latch, Touch) and submix tracks; the Mix track is where a final limiter or Loudness Meter belongs.
use_for: one EQ/compressor on a whole VO track
a music submix with one limiter
cards.how: Window > Audio Track Mixer > Show/Hide Effects and Sends > effect slot menu. Submixes: Sequence > Add Tracks. Automation writes track keyframes in the Timeline.
cards.script_api: Track.setMute(1)/isMuted() (ExtendScript), AudioTrack.setMute(bool)/isMuted() (UXP 25.6); track volume, pan, track effects and submix routing: none found
cards.limits: Track effects cannot be added by script, so automated chains must use clip effects (or nest the sequence and put effects on the nested clip: unverified). 'Write' automation mode did not work until 26.5, so in the installed 26.0.2 use Latch or Touch.

cards.name: Audio meters, Dynamic Audio Waveforms and Global Mute
cards.summary: Monitoring aids: Audio Meters (peak dBFS), waveforms that redraw with volume/keyframe/ducking changes (View > Dynamic Audio Waveforms) and live during trims, and muting of all/Source/Program playback: in the installed 26.0.2 via right-click on the Audio Meters (Mute All Audio / Mute Program Monitor); the menu-bar Global Mute button arrived in 26.2 (April 2026) and is not in 26.0.2.
cards.how: Window > Audio Meters; View > Dynamic Audio Waveforms (also scales with Audio Gain); mute: right-click the Audio Meters (26.0.2) or the menu-bar Global Mute button (26.2+); mute state is not saved with the project.
cards.script_api: none
cards.limits: Peak meters do not show LUFS: use the Loudness Meter or measure the export.

cards.name: Audio crossfade transitions (Constant Power, Constant Gain, Exponential Fade)
cards.summary: The three installed audio transitions. Constant Power = smooth equal-power crossfade (default choice), Constant Gain = linear, can dip mid-fade, Exponential Fade = logarithmic and more gradual.
use_for: smoothing audio edits between interview bites
1-4 frame fades to kill clicks at cuts
cards.how: Effects > Audio Transitions > Crossfade; drag onto the cut. Default: right-click > Set Selected As Default Transition; default duration in Preferences > Timeline > Audio Transition Default Duration. For custom curves use Volume keyframes instead.
cards.script_api: QE (unverified for audio): qeAudioTrackItem.addTransition(qe.project.getAudioTransitionByName('Constant Power'), ...); qe.project.getAudioTransitionList() is verified; UXP TransitionFactory only creates VIDEO transitions; verified route = Volume 'Level' keyframe fades (pr_build.jsx)
cards.limits: Needs media handles for a centred crossfade.

cards.name: Loudness Meter (and Loudness Radar)
cards.summary: TC Electronic ITU BS.1770 meter effect: Input (true-peak aware), Momentary (400 ms), Short-Term (3 s) and Integrated loudness, with presets for EBU R128, ATSC A/85 and online targets (YouTube, Spotify, Apple Podcasts, Netflix). Measures only, never changes audio. 'Loudness Radar' is the older TC radar-style meter, still installed.
use_for: checking a mix hits -14 LUFS / -1 dBTP before export
cards.how: Audio Track Mixer > Mix track > first effect slot > Special > Loudness Meter; double-click > Settings: Target Loudness, Low Level Below, Maximum True Peak, Scale (EBU +9 / +18), Unit (LKFS, LUFS, LU) or a preset. Play the whole sequence for Integrated.
cards.script_api: can be added to a clip via QE addAudioEffect('Loudness Meter') (done in the harvest) but readings are not exposed to scripts; its settings are the harvested params 'Target Level', 'Maximum True Peak', 'Scale', 'Unit', 'Low Below Level', 'Reset on Playback', 'Show Input/Short-Term/Integrated/Momentary Meter' (normalized 0..1, dB mapping unverified; the UI labels 'Target Loudness'/'Low Level Below' are NOT the script names); for automated QC measure the exported file instead (ffmpeg -af ebur128=peak=true, 0 credits)

cards.name: VO cleanup and mastering chain (recipe)

use_for: political news reels with music beds

cards.script_api: steps 1-5 via QE addAudioEffect + ComponentParam.setValue / Volume keyframes; step 6 via .epr edit; Enhance Speech, Auto Ducking, Auto-Match and track effects are UI-only
cards.limits: Numbers are common practice starting points, not Adobe specs; judge by ear. Noise reduction before compression; limiting last.

cards.name: Delivery loudness targets (YouTube, Instagram, broadcast)
cards.summary: Integrated loudness and true-peak targets for final mixes. YouTube: no official published spec; it turns loud uploads down toward about -14 LUFS and does not raise quiet ones (visible as 'content loudness' in Stats for nerds). Instagram/Facebook Reels: no published spec; community measurements point to about -14 LUFS. Ceiling -1 dBTP for lossy platforms (AES). Broadcast: EBU R128 -23 LUFS, ATSC A/85 -24 LKFS.
cards.how: Web/social deliveries: -14 LUFS integrated (acceptable -16..-13), true peak <= -1 dBTP; dialogue-led long-form can sit at -16 LUFS without being turned up by YouTube. Keep integrated above about -20 LUFS (bottom of the older AES TD1004 -16..-20 range; TD1008 warns that content quieter than its targets can be unsatisfyingly quiet on low-gain devices such as phones). Broadcast: follow the channel's spec sheet (R128 -23 LUFS or A/85 -24 LKFS; the export Loudness Normalization has both).
cards.script_api: Export Loudness Normalization via .epr XML (see that card); verify with ffmpeg -af ebur128=peak=true
cards.limits: YouTube/Instagram numbers are measured behaviour, not published specs, and can change. AES TD1008 (-18 LUFS speech, -16 music, -1 dBTP) is written for audio streaming, not sound-with-picture. See also: 'Documentary mix-level plan (dialogue, music, effects)'; 'Broadcast audio track layouts (EBU R 123)'; 'Stems and split-track export (dialogue, music, effects)'; 'Delivery spec: YouTube upload (16:9, HD and 4K)'; 'Delivery spec: vertical Reels, Shorts and TikTok (9:16)'; 'Delivery spec: broadcast masters (ProRes 422 HQ, XDCAM HD422 MXF OP1a)'.

cards.name: Audio Levels (layer property)
cards.summary: Every AE layer with audio has Audio > Audio Levels, a [left, right] pair in dB; keyframe it for fades and ducks inside a comp.
use_for: fading SFX/music inside an AE comp
balancing whooshes against a title animation
cards.how: Timeline: select layer, press L (Audio Levels) or LL (waveform). Script: layer.property("ADBE Audio Group").property("ADBE Audio Levels").setValueAtTime(t, [dB, dB]); layer.audioEnabled = true/false toggles the speaker switch.
cards.script_api: AVLayer.property('ADBE Audio Group').property('ADBE Audio Levels').setValue([l, r]) / setValueAtTime(t, [l, r]); AVLayer.hasAudio, audioEnabled (r/w), audioActive, audioActiveAtTime(t)
cards.limits: AE has no loudness meter or mixer: do the final mix in Premiere. Audio from a Dynamic-Linked comp arrives in Premiere already mixed by these levels.

cards.name: Compressor
cards.summary: New (2026) AE audio compressor: Threshold (dB) -60..0 (default -16), Ratio (x:1) 0.4..30 (3), Knee (db) 0..30 (15), Attack (ms) 0..400 (6), Release (ms) 1..4000 (440), Auto Release (on), Makeup Gain (dB) -30..30, Output Limit (dB) -30..0 (-1).
use_for: evening out a VO or SFX layer that lives in an AE comp
cards.how: Effect > Audio > Compressor. Spec: {"name": "ADBE Aud Compressor", "props": {"Threshold (dB)": -20, "Ratio (x:1)": 3, "Makeup Gain (dB)": 4, "Output Limit (dB)": -1}}. Adobe tip: dialogue 3:1 fast attack; music 2:1-4:1 slower attack.
cards.script_api: layer.property('ADBE Effect Parade').addProperty('ADBE Aud Compressor') then setValue on the named props
cards.limits: Release is ignored while 'Auto Release' = 1. Property name 'Knee (db)' has a lowercase 'db'. Added in the 2026 cycle (beta 26.0x8, then release; present in the installed AE 26.0 harvest): not in AE 2024/2025.

cards.name: Gate
cards.summary: New (2026) AE noise gate: Threshold (dB) -60..0 (default -60), Attack (ms) 0..1000 (10), Hold (ms) 0..2500 (40), Release (ms) 5..4000 (220).
use_for: cutting hiss between words on a layer in AE
cards.how: Effect > Audio > Gate; raise Threshold until the noise between phrases disappears. Spec: {"name": "ADBE Aud Gate", "props": {"Threshold (dB)": -45, "Release (ms)": 150}}.
cards.script_api: addProperty('ADBE Aud Gate') + setValue
cards.limits: Too high a threshold chops word tails; default -60 dB does almost nothing.

cards.name: Distortion
cards.summary: New (2026) AE distortion + bitcrusher: Type 1-6 (Soft Clip, Hard Clip, Saturation 1, Saturation 2, Tube, Fuzz), Drive 0..100 (25), Gain 0..300 (25), Mix 0..100 (100), Volume 0..100 (11), Resolution (bit) 1..24 (24), Downsample (x) 1..48 (1).
use_for: lo-fi glitch SFX for tech reels
cards.how: Effect > Audio > Distortion. Radio voice: {"name": "ADBE Aud Distortion", "props": {"Type": 2, "Drive": 50, "Mix": 60}} plus High-Low Pass; lo-fi: Resolution (bit) 8, Downsample (x) 4.
cards.script_api: addProperty('ADBE Aud Distortion') + setValue
cards.limits: Volume default 11 is low-ish; check levels after. Type dropdown order taken from Adobe's list.

cards.name: High-Low Pass
cards.summary: Single high-pass or low-pass filter with Cutoff Frequency 1..20000 Hz (default 2000) and Dry/Wet Out.
use_for: muffled 'behind the wall' or underwater voice (low pass)
thin phone voice (two instances: HP ~300 Hz + LP ~3400 Hz)
sweeping a filter into a drop
cards.how: Effect > Audio > High-Low Pass. Filter Options 1 = High Pass, 2 = Low Pass (order as in the UI list; verify). For a filter, Dry Out 0 and Wet Out 100. Animate Cutoff Frequency for sweeps.
cards.script_api: var fx = layer.property('ADBE Effect Parade').addProperty('ADBE Aud HiLo'); fx.property('Filter Options').setValue(2); fx.property('Cutoff Frequency').setValueAtTime(t, hz)
cards.limits: Gentle slope; for steep phone EQ stack two.

cards.name: Parametric EQ
cards.summary: Three-band peaking EQ (Band 1/2/3 Enabled, Frequency 1..21609 Hz, Bandwidth 0.1..99, Boost/Cut -100..100) with a response graph.
use_for: cutting a whine or rumble in an AE-only audio layer
cards.how: Effect > Audio > Parametric EQ; band 1 on by default (1000 Hz), bands 2-3 off (5000 / 10000 Hz).
cards.script_api: addProperty('ADBE Param EQ'); bands 2-3 share property names with band 1, so address them by index (effect.property(n)) rather than by name
cards.limits: Property names repeat per band ('Frequency', 'Bandwidth', 'Boost/Cut'), so a PVE spec addressing them by name is ambiguous; harvested default Boost/Cut is 50 and its unit is not documented (test by ear). Usually better done in Premiere.

cards.name: Reverb (AE)
cards.summary: Simple algorithmic reverb: Reverb Time (ms) 0..5000 (100), Diffusion 0..100 (75), Decay 0..100 (25), Brightness 0..100 (10), Dry Out 0..400 (90), Wet Out 0..400 (10).
use_for: tails on trailer hits and whooshes inside a comp
cards.how: Effect > Audio > Reverb; raise Decay for bigger spaces. Delay ('ADBE Aud Delay') is the echo counterpart.
cards.script_api: addProperty('ADBE Aud Reverb') + setValue
cards.limits: Low quality next to Premiere's Studio/Convolution Reverb; fine for SFX.

cards.name: Tone
cards.summary: Synthesizes up to five tones (Frequency 1-5 Hz, Level 0..100 default 20, Waveform options 1-5) on any layer, even a solid; original audio is ignored.
use_for: censor bleep in AE (single 1000 Hz sine)
UI blips and data beeps for tech/news graphics
cards.how: Effect > Audio > Tone. Turn off unused tones by setting their Frequency to 0; keep Level <= 100 / number of tones; keyframe Level to 0 on the last frame to avoid a click.
cards.script_api: var fx = layer.property('ADBE Effect Parade').addProperty('ADBE Aud Tone'); fx.property('Frequency 2').setValue(0) etc.
cards.limits: 'Waveform options' 1-5 covers Sine, Triangle, Saw, Square, White Noise (Adobe's list); default 1 = sine is likely, the order of 2-5 is unverified: test by ear. No sound on placeholder layers.

cards.name: De-esser (AE beta)
cards.summary: Sibilance reducer being tested in After Effects (beta): Threshold, Frequency (default 7000 Hz), Bandwidth (3000 Hz), Attack (1 ms), Release (50 ms), Sibilance Only.
use_for: harsh S on VO kept inside AE
cards.how: AE (beta) only. Adobe starting points: narration about -20 dB / 7 kHz / 3 kHz / 1 ms / 50-100 ms; deeper male voice -18 dB / 4-5 kHz.
cards.script_api: unverified (not in the installed AE 2026 harvest; match name unknown)
cards.limits: Not in release AE 2026 as harvested on 2026-10-03; use Premiere's DeEsser.

cards.name: Convert Audio to Keyframes
cards.summary: Keyframe assistant that creates an 'Audio Amplitude' null with sliders 'Left Channel', 'Right Channel', 'Both Channels' keyed every frame from the comp's audio, for audio-reactive motion.
use_for: pulsing logos/text to the VO or music
cards.how: Select the audio layer > Animation > Keyframe Assistant > Convert Audio to Keyframes. Drive a property with linear(thisComp.layer("Audio Amplitude").effect("Both Channels")("Slider"), 0, peak, minVal, maxVal).
cards.script_api: unverified: select the layer, then app.executeCommand(app.findMenuCommandId("Convert Audio to Keyframes")) (both functions are documented; the command name lookup is not verified here); fallback = build the null yourself from an offline amplitude analysis and setValuesAtTimes
cards.limits: Uses the whole comp's audio (all audible layers), not one layer: solo or precompose first. Amplitude values are arbitrary units: remap with linear().

cards.name: Audio Spectrum and Audio Waveform (visualizers)
cards.summary: Generate effects that draw a frequency spectrum (ADBE AudSpect) or waveform (ADBE AudWave) from an audio layer, optionally along a mask path.
use_for: VO waveform under a speaker name
cards.how: Apply to a solid; set Audio Layer to the music/VO layer; Start/End Point (pixels) or a Path; Spectrum: Start/End Frequency, Frequency bands, Maximum Height, Display Options 1-3; Waveform: Displayed Samples, Maximum Height. Spec example: {"name": "ADBE AudSpect", "props": {"Frequency bands": 48, "Maximum Height": 600, "Inside Color": "#FFFFFF"}}.
cards.script_api: props settable by name except 'Audio Layer' (layer type) and 'Path' (mask type), which a PVE spec cannot set; set them in ExtendScript: effect.property('Audio Layer').setValue(layerIndex) and effect.property('Path').setValue(maskIndex) (PropertyValueType LAYER_INDEX / MASK_INDEX are integers, 0 = none, per the AE scripting guide)
cards.limits: Reads the source footage audio without time remapping, effects, stretch or levels: precompose the audio layer if those must show.

cards.name: After Effects audio output and limits
cards.summary: AE is not a mixing tool: legacy-quality audio effects (plus the 2026 Compressor/Gate/Distortion), no loudness meter, no ducking, no noise reduction. Render audio comes from the Output Module.
use_for: deciding where audio work happens (answer: Premiere)
rendering an AE comp with or without audio
cards.how: Keep VO and music in Premiere; in AE keep only SFX tied to animation. Enable audio output in the Output Module (Audio Output on/off, sample rate, channels). For scripted renders, read the exact keys with outputModule.getSettings(GetSettingsFormat.STRING_SETTABLE) before calling setSettings.
cards.script_api: OutputModule.getSettings(GetSettingsFormat.STRING_SETTABLE) / setSettings({...}) (audio key names unverified: read them first)
cards.limits: Audio preview in AE needs RAM preview; Dynamic Link passes AE audio into Premiere already mixed.
